subject.title: TUI: Support inline image display in iTerm2 / Kitty / Sixel terminals

question: Should OpenClaw core implement TUI inline rendering for image tool results now, and what terminal-protocol, local media-read, fallback, and config boundary should that implementation use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature adds terminal graphics behavior, possible local file reads, and a requested config surface that require maintainer product and safety direction before automation can safely implement or land it.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core TUI implementation
options.body: Use the open draft as input, but require a rebase, current dependency imports, explicit trusted-media rules, no unnecessary config surface, focused TUI tests, and live Kitty/iTerm2 proof before merge.

options.title: Defer terminal graphics support
options.body: Keep the placeholder fallback as current behavior and close or park the linked draft until terminal graphics becomes a priority.

options.title: Split config from rendering
options.body: Land capability-detected rendering first only if maintainers reject a new setting, then open a separate config discussion if users need an override.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core TUI implementation
recommendation.body: Use the open draft as input, but require a rebase, current dependency imports, explicit trusted-media rules, no unnecessary config surface, focused TUI tests, and live Kitty/iTerm2 proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current TUI renderer and adjacent image-generation work both point to this owner as the best available routing candidate for the product boundary decision.
